applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, amended by 2009 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended; Art. 627a of the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220), as revised by the 2015 UBO register reform; Art. 632-633 CO on minimum subscribed capital of CHF 100,000 and minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033.0) for payment intermediaries; Art. 305bis-305ter of the Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) on money laundering offenses.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - the UBO register under CO Art. 627a is an internal corporate record naming every direct or indirect beneficial owner of more than 25% of voting rights or capital; it is not filed publicly and is accessible only to competent authorities (FINMA, MROS, cantonal tax and audit offices), to shareholders holding over 0.5% of capital, and to creditors with an enforceable judgment.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the registry state's competent authority, followed by a certified German or French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Swiss notary, incorporator and fiduciary agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized board resolution of the corporate shareholder or the individual shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; notarized counter-signature by residential notary where apostille is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state notary, embassy or consulate in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for jurisdictions outside the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by the issuing bank with signature specimen; apostille not ordinarily required, subject to notary discretion

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Individual director self-declaration countersigned by the cantonal notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature recognition before the Swiss notary; apostille not required for locally notarized declarations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory bidirectional screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against the SECO consolidated Swiss sanctions list implementing UN and EU measures, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the EU consolidated financial sanctions list. Politically exposed persons are identified under CO Art. 627a and GwG Art. 12a-12b; enhanced due diligence applies where a PEP resides in a high-risk jurisdiction or where payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments) classify the account as higher risk. The non-financial manufacturer is not a regulated intermediary under GwG, but its UBO declarations must be primed for inspection by FINMA-authorized auditors and by acquiring banks during merchant underwriting.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Index (Zentraler Firmenindex / Index central des raisons de société), operated by the Swiss Federal Office of Justice, with formal name pre-clearance filed at the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin script and must be legible in at least one Swiss official language (German, French or Italian), in accordance with CO Arts. 950-951. An English or trademark-style brand token is admissible as the distinctive part of the name provided the legal-form suffix AG or SA is appended, the name is not misleading about the nature of the business, and it does not violate Swissness provisions (Trade Mark Protection Act, SR 232.11). Non-Latin brand scripts require a registered Latin transliteration for Swiss use and for Zefix publication.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss, Schweiz, Suisse, Svizzera, Helvetia, and the Swiss cross (Swissness Act arts. 35-37, ministerial authorization required)
Bank, Banque, Banca, Insurance, Versicherung, Assurance
Lawyer, Rechtsanwalt, Avocat, Attorney, Notary, Notar
University, Hochschule, Institut (where misrepresenting academic status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon provisional refusal, the incorporator may request a written statement of grounds from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, file a revised name for fresh pre-clearance, or appeal to the cantonal supervisory authority under Arts. 29-35 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) within 30 days of notification. A further appeal on questions of law lies to the Federal Administrative Court. Cantons offering pre-clearance retain an accepted name for 30 days, with extension possible in certain cantons upon payment of an additional fee; if incorporation is not completed within the reservation window, the name lapses and the process restarts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted - a pure letterbox or PO-box-only address is not accepted. CO Art. 626(1) requires the articles of association to designate the registered seat as a specific Swiss municipality, and the Cantonal Commercial Register Office will verify the existence of a physical office where legal correspondence, corporate records and UBO registers are kept. For an e-commerce manufacturer, a serviced office or shared commercial workspace in Zug, Zurich or Geneva with a visible company sign, lockable filing space and full-time receptionist is acceptable; a fully virtual desktop-only arrangement is not recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% for a low-risk, non-licensed e-commerce goods manufacturer at the incorporation stage. Probability rises to roughly 30% if the registered office is a serviced address without an appointed in-country correspondence agent, if customs or trademark complaints arise, or if any UBO or director appears on sanctions or PEP-adjacent watchlists. Cantonal auditors and tax authorities are entitled to unannounced physical inspection to confirm commercial substance under the Federal Act on Mergers and Commercial Register (SR 221.411).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry for the Aktiengesellschaft, including federal Zefix publication and cantonal registration fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory scale under cantonal fee ordinances: CHF 400-900 total for incorporation entry, plus CHF 40-90 federal publication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of four foreign corporate and personal documents for the non-resident shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international tariff of USD 40-110 per apostille depending on the issuing state; no Swiss federal fee applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified German or French translation of foreign articles, powers of attorney, UBO declarations and register extracts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss sworn translation bureau or court-certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 30-60 per standard page; estimated total CHF 300-450 for approximately 10 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Standard legal and fiduciary advisory retainer for Stage-1 pre-incorporation coordination, UBO piercing and AML file assembly
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 250-400 per hour or flat-stage fee of CHF 1,700-2,800, excluding VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Private market benchmark for a small meeting-ready unit of 12-20 square meters in a business center, CHF 900-1,400 per month inclusive of utilities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), as revised effective 1 January 2023; Swiss Civil Code Art. 52 (legal personality); Federal Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV, SR 221.411); Federal Act on Labour in Industry, Commerce and Trade (Arbeitsgesetz, ArG), Art. 7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton, acting with a cantonally recognized notary public for the public deed; supervised by the Federal Office for the Commercial Register (FEDRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung des Errichtungsakts) with the Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted through the Commercial Register application form (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG requires a minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (Art. 632 OR). At incorporation, at least CHF 20,000 must be paid up in cash and deposited on a blocked share-capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank; the bank's confirmation that the funds are at the free disposal of the Board is a mandatory filing condition. The unpaid balance remains callable by the Board of Directors and must be fully paid in the event of insolvency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. Share Subscription and Allotment. The Board acknowledges the subscription of 1,000 registered shares, nominal value CHF 100 each, totalling CHF 100,000. The statutory minimum payment of CHF 20,000 has been deposited to the blocked share account, and the bank certificate confirming free disposal of the funds is hereby accepted. The shares are allotted and issued in accordance with the Articles of Association. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [City], [Canton], Switzerland. The Board approves the lease of these premises and confirms them as the statutory seat. 3. Appointment of Officers. The Board appoints [Name], [Name] and [Name] as directors. [Name] is elected President. [Name] and [Name] are granted individual, and [Name] joint, signatory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Certification of the Founding Documents (Public Deed and Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonally recognized civil-law notary public (öffentliche Urkundsperson / notaire public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear in person before the chosen notary with valid identity documents. The notary reviews the draft Articles of Association, verifies board composition and the capital payment certificate, reads the deed aloud, and obtains the signatures of each founder. The notary certifies the signatures, retains the original notarial record, and issues certified copies for the registry filing. The deed must contain the declarations prescribed by Art. 640 OR, including the capital payment confirmation, the organizational clause, and the representation clause.
required_dossiers: Valid identity documents (passport or Swiss ID) of each founder
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Blocked share-capital account certificate issued by a Swiss bank (Bestätigung der eingezahlten Gelder)
Draft founding deed (Errichtungsakt) prepared by the notary
Authenticated power of attorney if any founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a founder identifies a defect, the deed is redrafted and a new execution session is convened; the defective instrument is cancelled and replaced before lodging fees are incurred, minimizing additional cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Publication of the Swiss Stock Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton, with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of the notarial deed, the Board of Directors or its authorized representative submits the registration application to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office. The application must include the signed declaration that the paid-up capital is at the free disposal of the Board and that the statutory conditions are fulfilled. The registry examines the deed for compliance; upon entry, the company acquires legal personality under Art. 643 OR, and the entry is published in the SHAB.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized founding deed
Commercial Register application form (Anmeldung) signed by the Board of Directors
Board declaration on the free disposal of paid-up capital, dated no more than three business days before filing
Notarized specimen signatures (Unterschriftenproben) of all authorized signatories
Power of attorney for the filing representative if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a rectification request, the applicant cures by supplying the missing declaration or document within the granted period (usually 10-30 days). If registration is refused, an administrative appeal may be filed with the cantonal supervisory authority or the competent cantonal court within 30 days; alternatively, a corrected application may be resubmitted as a new filing after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Company Data Procurement: UID, VAT Number and Authorized Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV) through the QuickForm and ESS portal; SHAB publication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the SHAB publication, the Board obtains a certified Commercial Register extract and the enterprise identification number (UID) from the Federal Tax Administration. The company must assess whether its annual global turnover exceeds the VAT registration threshold of CHF 250,000 or whether voluntary VAT registration is economically beneficial for input-tax deduction on injection molding machinery. UID and VAT registration are applied for electronically via the FTA portal using the Commercial Register extract.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
SHAB publication confirmation
Online FTA registration form for UID and VAT (QuickForm)
Copy of the Articles of Association
Board resolution electing the VAT filing mode if voluntary registration is chosen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The UID is issued automatically following registry data transfer, even if VAT processing is delayed. Any delayed VAT registration is cured by prompt self-disclosure with the FTA, and a formal assessment may be appealed within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration Under Social Security Law (AHV, SUVA and Pension Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) of the seat canton and the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the first salary payment, the company must register as an employer with the competent AHV Compensation Office and enroll its employees. Mandatory occupational and non-occupational accident insurance (UVG) must be contracted with SUVA or a licensed private insurer within 14 days after recruitment. The company must file payroll data, working-time arrangements, and the responsible employer contact. Affiliation with a professional pension fund (BVG) is then completed through the compensation office or the selected pension institution.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Employer registration form of the Cantonal Compensation Office
List of employees with AHV insurance numbers and salary data
SUVA or licensed-insurer accident insurance application
Completed social security questionnaire (Fragebogen) of the Compensation Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration is cured by immediate retroactive enrollment; unpaid AHV contributions may attract interest, but penalties are generally waived upon voluntary disclosure. SUVA coverage is effective from the policy application date even if administrative processing is delayed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV / AFC), VAT Division, Schwarztorstrasse 50, CH-3003 Bern; centralized Swiss VAT registration and compliance portal at https://estv.admin.ch (SuisseTax eServices). Switzerland applies a unitary national VAT system; cantonal and communal authorities administer direct profit taxes only and have no VAT competence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the resident CH_AG: after commercial register incorporation, the FTA issues the UID business identification number (format CHE-116.345.890), which is converted ex officio into a VAT number by adding the suffix 'MWST' once the AG notifies the start of taxable activity (Form 1425 via FTA e-services) and meets the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold or opts for voluntary registration. VAT registration is effective from commencement of the taxable activity; the MWST ID is typically issued within 2 to 4 weeks. Non-Swiss entities without a Swiss establishment appoint a Swiss tax representative (jointly and severally liable, Art. 67 para 2 MWSTG) and apply through the FTA portal; foreign suppliers of electronic B2C services may instead use the simplified national notification procedure applicable since 1 January 2025.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Aktiengesellschaft (AG / SA, Swiss stock company) is a resident capital company subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide profits and capital: federal profit tax at 8.5% on after-tax profit, plus cantonal/communal profit tax (effective aggregate approximately 12% to 24% depending on canton). No pass-through or fiscal transparency applies. Territorial scope: profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt at the cantonal/communal level with progression and relieved under double taxation treaties at the federal level; for VAT, the AG is a Swiss taxable person with an establishment for all goods and services supplied in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, partnership classification or S-corp election exists in Swiss law. Relevant elections for a custom-manufacturing AG: (1) VAT group taxation for closely linked enterprises (Art. 52 MWSTG, binding for at least five tax periods) to consolidate the keycap production entity with sister sales companies; (2) opt-in to VAT liability below the CHF 100,000 threshold (Art. 11 para 4 MWSTG); (3) option to subject real estate letting to VAT (Art. 22 para 2 MWSTG); (4) OECD hybrid mismatch deduction-limitation rules (in force since 1 January 2020) disallow deductions where the counterparty does not include the corresponding income; (5) OECD Pillar Two GloBE top-up tax (IIR/UTPR at 15%) applies from fiscal year 2024 to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss federal Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG, SR 641.20); a multi-stage, credit-invoice, destination-based consumption tax with reverse charge for cross-border services and an explicit tax exemption threshold for small enterprises; Switzerland is not an EU member and does not apply EU VAT directives.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies linked to Switzerland (Art. 10 para 2 lit. a MWSTG). The threshold applies to Swiss-resident and non-resident suppliers alike; exports of goods (0% supplies) count toward the threshold. Enterprises below the threshold are exempt but may register voluntarily (Art. 11 MWSTG).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory continuous transaction control, no real-time fiscal clearance and no digital stamping regime exists. Invoices may be paper or electronic; mandatory content under Art. 26 MWSTG applies to invoices exceeding CHF 400 (supplier UID, recipient, nature/date/amount of supply and applicable VAT rate or zero-rating reference). The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung, SIX standard) is the mandatory structured payment instrument in the Swiss receivables workflow since 30 June 2020; voluntary B2B e-invoicing via Peppol BIS 3.0 and B2C Swiss eBill is permitted. Export invoices must reference the customs MRN and state 'Export supply, zero-rated under Art. 23 MWSTG'; no API clearance or government pre-approval is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports are zero-rated under Art. 23 para 1 MWSTG when: (i) the goods physically leave Switzerland to a foreign destination; (ii) dispatch/transport is performed by the supplier, the buyer or a third party; (iii) the recipient is established outside Switzerland or the goods terminate in a foreign customs territory; and (iv) the exporter holds verifiable customs, transport and payment evidence. CH_AG's double-shot PBT keycap shipments to non-Swiss final customers and distributors qualify as 0% supplies upon proof of export; ancillary services directly connected with the export (freight, handling, commissions) also benefit from the 0% rate under Art. 23 para 2 MWSTG. Deliveries to Swiss customers, supplies consumed in Switzerland, and goods merely warehoused in Switzerland before a later re-export remain taxable at the ordinary 8.1% or reduced 2.6% rate; EU/UK distance sales may trigger foreign VAT registration and import schemes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration in e-dec/NCTS with Movement Reference Number (MRN) proving physical exit from Swiss customs territory
Commercial invoice stating exporter UID/MWST number, consignee, Incoterms, HS code (e.g., 3926.90 or 8471.60), quantity, value and the declaration 'Export supply, zero-rated under Art. 23 MWSTG'
Transport document - original bill of lading, air waybill (AWB), CMR consignment note or rail waybill evidencing delivery to the foreign consignee and destination
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT transfer instruction / card-settlement statement evidencing receipt of foreign-currency proceeds in the CH_AG's bank account
Recipient evidence - foreign VAT ID, company register extract or residence/IP proof for private buyers confirming non-Swiss status
Transaction file - purchase order, sales contract, insurance certificates and delivery acceptance notes forming the complete audit trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Switzerland imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark stated herein is an internal control threshold for timely export substantiation and aligns with FTA audit practice of matching export declarations against bank receipts within the accounting year. FTA post-clearance export audits may reassess VAT at 8.1% on the invoice value where zero-rating is unproven, plus default interest at 5% per annum and clawback of any input VAT allocated to the fictitious export. Criminal exposure: intentional tax evasion under Art. 58 MWSTG is punishable by a fine up to CHF 100,000 (negligent: up to CHF 10,000); fraudulent use of forged export documents constitutes Abgabebetrug under Art. 59 MWSTG and Swiss customs criminal law, with imprisonment up to five years (up to ten years in qualified aggravated cases with large amounts). The normal five-year limitation for VAT assessment is extended to ten years in cases of evasion or fraud (Art. 42 para 3 MWSTG). Export vouchers and books must be retained for ten years (Art. 89 MWSTG).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank, Banque Nationale Suisse, Banca Nazionale Svizzera); currency and monetary policy is implemented without an exchange-control authority and there is no separate foreign-exchange administration in Switzerland. The State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and FINMA share policy and supervision functions, respectively.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full currency convertibility on both the current account and the capital account. The Swiss franc is freely convertible, with no restrictions on remittance of dividends, interest, royalties, or returns of capital to non-residents. Profit repatriation by an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is effected through board-approved dividend distributions, subject to the statutory annual general meeting approval process, applicable statutory profit availability tests, and, where relevant, Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at 35% on distributions to non-qualifying shareholders; a reduced rate may apply under a double taxation treaty. There is no statutory foreign-exchange allocation, priority-rationing system, or MAC-clause blocking of dividend transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender rule exists under Swiss law. Exporters are not required to repatriate foreign-currency proceeds within any statutory timeline and are not required to convert export revenues into CHF. Export receivables may be retained in foreign currency, netted, or converted at the company's discretion, subject only to general bookkeeping and Swiss Federal Tax Administration reporting of taxable income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Kontokorrent/Kapitalkonto) and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability for offshore digital EMIs acting as primary treasury accounts. A Swiss AG requires an account with a bank or FINMA-licensed fintech institution holding a banking licence or deposit-holding authorisation. Offshore EMIs not licensed or passported into Switzerland cannot legally maintain customer accounts in CHF or provide settlement infrastructure without an onward clearing relationship. A licensed Swiss fintech such as a FINMA 'fintech licence' holder or a Swiss bank with a full banking licence may be used as a low-cost digital treasury intermediary, but the legal settlement layer must remain a regulated Swiss financial intermediary. For Shopify Payments and Stripe receiving channels, the merchant account will be routed through Stripe/Shopify's respective acquiring banking partners; this does not replace the need for a Swiss-authorised settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In almost all Swiss tier-1 banks, at least one board member and the director (or the authorised signatory) must physically appear at a bank branch or at the attorney-trustee's office for the final identity verification and source-of-funds interview. Remote onboarding is permitted only in limited circumstances using FINMA-compliant video-identification and digital signature processes, but it usually remains subject to higher due diligence scrutiny. For a newly incorporated AG, the expectation is an in-person or video-interview with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), provision of legalised or certified corporate documents, and a clear commercial explanation for the cross-border trade flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution from foreign individual shareholders without transparent source-of-wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board resolution for share capital payment; certified copy of the deed of incorporation and articles of incorporation; bank statement or SWIFT confirmation of the capital remittance; notarised affidavit of source of wealth of each shareholder; three months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder; tax residence certificates; copy of powers of attorney and passport copies certified by competent authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque cross-border e-commerce settlement flows through PSPs and payment facilitators with no auditable trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed payment processor agreements (Stripe, Shopify Payments); processed-transaction reconciliation reports per payout event; customer identifying data and order logs; delivery and customs documentation for each major consignment; audited annual financial statement and VAT/GST filing evidence; a written AML/KYC procedure manual for customer due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern that trade payments to Asian suppliers exceed invoice values or are routed through unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, and final commercial invoices; full BOM costing and per-unit manufacturing cost breakdown; sea/air waybill and bill of lading readouts; customs declarations; supplier KYC file including official business registration, bank confirmation, and beneficial owner declaration; independent audit confirmation of trade margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected nominee or indirect shareholder ownership without clear UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial register extract with UBO declarations; signed declaration of no nominal shareholding; organisational chart showing full ownership chain to final natural persons; shareholder register; passport copies and proof of address of each UBO; if corporate shareholders, their constituent documents and source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared low-risk manufacturing activity and unexpected large transactions among interns or foreign counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved annual budget and cash-flow forecast; signed contracts with counterparties; proof of trade finance or treasury approval framework; internal treasury policy; invoice-level verification through third-party trade verification; confirmation of final product use and no dual-use barred categories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound CHF or foreign-currency equity injections shall be wired via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) to the Swiss clearing bank using standard SIC/SEPA mechanics. The payment order must reference the company full legal name, the corporate account number, and the purpose code for direct investment / equity capital (e.g., 'CAP/ EQU-01', 'Direct Investment' or 'BOP 4078' if requested by the receiving bank; in Switzerland there is no mandatory central-bank purpose code but commercial banks may use OECD/IMF classification for statistics). Receiving bank documentation shall include board resolution, share issuance minutes, capital adequacy calculation, UBO declarations, and the certified share register. No prior exchange-control approval is required, but violation-free onboarding requires the capital injection to be neat, traceable, and line-by-line reconcilable with the company's treasury file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for injection-moulded keycaps will be executed through SIC-CH/EuroSIC or the SWIFT network. Best practice for supplier settlements uses SWIFT MT103 for non-recurring USD/EUR/CNY/CHF disbursements and irrevocable commercial letters of credit (Documentary Credits) for large repeat purchase orders from Asian contract manufacturers. For Swiss and European payroll, rents, and domestic operating expense, SEPA Direct Debit and CHF direct clearing through SIC are mandatory. Supplier invoices below USD 50,000 shall be paid by MT103 within the standard SWIFT window; invoices above USD 50,000 or requiring legal internet will use the Commercial LC corridor with documents against payment. No foreign-exchange liquidation or surrender approval is triggered, but each outgoing transfer must accurately state the purpose code, and sanctions screening must be performed for all counterparties before initiating payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards on CHF/EUR/USD/CNY for up to 12-month tenors with a licensed Swiss banking counterparty
FX swaps for shifting maturity of cross-currency cash inflows and outflows
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for longer than 12-month repatriation of foreign-currency capital or trade exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically permitted but are rarely needed for CHF given full convertibility; they may be used only with approved international banks and must be booked through the Swiss treasury clearing desk; no exchange-control permit applies
Options and swaps in the form of barrier strategies are permissible for treasury hedging but are not recommended as a standalone derivative absent board approval and appropriate risk documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and audit report filing for Aktiengesellschaft
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC) via competent cantonal tax authority; Commercial Register Office of the canton of registered office (e.g., Zug Commercial Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for calendar-year companies, by 30 June of the following year; cantonal tax return deadlines may extend to 31 March or 31 May per canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties from cantonal tax authority (typically CHF 100–5,000); interest at 4.5% per annum on unpaid taxes; repeated non-compliance may trigger official warning and administrative enforcement, but commercial register strike-off applies only after formal liquidation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting approval of annual financial statements and appropriation of profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders' meeting; minutes recorded in corporate records; no filing to Commercial Register unless capital changes or board changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for calendar-year companies, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine; failure to hold meeting may lead to civil liability of board members, loss of discharge, and court-ordered convocation upon shareholder petition

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax return and tax balance sheet / income statement filing for corporate income tax, cantonal tax, and communal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (e.g., Zug Cantonal Tax Office) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal deadline typically 31 March for prior calendar year; extension available upon written request to 30 June / 30 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% per annum; cantonal penalties up to CHF 10,000 for negligent non-payment or late filing; intentional tax evasion penalties up to three times the evaded tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (value added tax) filing and payment; annual VAT settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC) VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If filing quarterly: within 60 days after the end of each quarter; if filing annually: within 60 days after the end of the business year; annual turnover threshold permitting annual filing exceeded by keyboard cap manufacturer generating over CHF 100,000 taxable turnover
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 4.5% per annum on arrears; penalty for late filing of 10% of the VAT due if not remitted on time; deliberate evasion subject to additional fines and criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual salary register and social security contribution declaration (AVS / AHV, ALV, BVG, UVG) for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Zug / Compenswiss Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse) and Swiss Social Security authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly contribution payments due within 60 days after each quarter; annual wage declaration by 30 January following the reporting year or per fund deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 5% per annum on unpaid contributions; administrative fines of up to double the unpaid amount; directors' personal liability for withheld but unremitted employees' social security contributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office and corporate metadata to the Commercial Register / publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canton Zug Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No statutory anniversary filing; mandatory filing occurs only upon changes to directors, registered office, capital, or statutes; annual register confirmation not separately required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file required changes within statutory period may incur administrative penalty up to CHF 5,000 and removal of company if insolvent after formal liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner disclosure / UBO register confirmation to the beneficial ownership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Registry of Beneficial Owners (register maintained by the Federal Department of Justice and Police); filed through e-government portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 60 days of incorporation or acquisition of significant control; annual confirmation only when shareholding changes; for stability, report no later than 31 December after a change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to CHF 100,000; criminal penalties for intentional false declarations; for the same entry, fine applies to directors and officers; repeated violations may lead to criminal conviction and directors' disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of accident insurance and occupational compliance for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (Suva) or private accident insurer; cantonal labor inspectorate only upon obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual premium statement submitted within 30 days after policy anniversary; mandatory for all employees including part-time and home workers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Insurer surcharges and civil liability; failure to insure employees is a criminal offense under Swiss Accident Insurance Act with fines up to CHF 20,000; directors personally liable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit required for Swiss AG if two of three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, employees 250 FTEs; limited audit (Review) required if thresholds not met unless shareholders unanimously waive by opting-out with 100% consent; unlimited audit exemption unavailable under Code of Obligations art. 727 for AG
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting provisions with Swiss GAAP FER for true and fair view statutory accounts; Irish-style IFRS not mandatory; IFRS accounting permitted but not required for statutory filing; SME financial reporting under OR 957–963b

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains a central register of beneficial owners (RDB) accessed only by authorities; company must file legal entities and natural persons owning >25% of shares or control; annual confirmation not required on a fixed date, but any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 60 days; fusion of shareholding transfers into an annual confirmation is accepted; director is obliged to keep an internal register of shareholders and report UBO changes
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / Management and Auditors
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings
Register of Capital Increases and Repayments
General internal ledger with bank confirmations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,500–4,500 (USD 1,700–5,000) for Swiss registered agent / domicile service per annum
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited review: CHF 2,000–5,000 (USD 2,300–5,800); full statutory audit: CHF 8,000–25,000 (USD 9,300–29,000) in Zug market

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% flat federal corporate income tax on net profit; combined Zug cantonal and communal headline rate approximately 11.8% for an Aktiengesellschaft.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF 2020 incentives in Zug: patent box relief on qualifying IP income with up to 90% exclusion, 150% R&D super-deduction, participation exemption for dividends and capital gains on qualifying holdings of at least 10%, ZUG notional interest deduction on qualifying excess equity, and no special wealth tax surcharge beyond ordinary Zug capital tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return Steuererklärung fuer juristische Personen filed with the Zuger Steuerverwaltung through the WINBEZ electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; quarterly prepayment installments of estimated current-year tax due 31 March, 30 June, 30 September, and 31 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the commercial fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the Zug administration generally requires filing by 31 March and routinely grants an automatic extension to 30 September.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gewinn oder Verlust laut Erfolgsrechnung: net business profit or loss before taxes per the statutory income statement prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Swiss-source profit attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment or Swiss real estate; all intercompany allocations must follow OECD arm's-length standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aufrechnungen: tax additions for non-deductible expenses, including hidden profit distributions, excess financing costs, non-business-related commissions, accrued taxes, and unjustified write-downs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must add back the same non-deductible items to the permanent establishment profit and maintain full evidence of the Swiss PE cost accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Kuerzungen: tax deductions including participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, patent box income exclusion, R&D super-deduction, and deemed notional interest deduction on Zug excess equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim participation relief only when the foreign participation is treaty-protected and the 10% threshold or CHF 1 million book-value test is documented; the DTA entitlement must be supported by a valid tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Steuerbarer Reingewinn: taxable net profit forming the base for federal and cantonal income tax after adjustments in Boxes 1.2 and 1.3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies the taxable base is limited to the Swiss permanent establishment profit and Swiss real estate income; no worldwide consolidation is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Steuerbares Kapital: taxable capital base for the Zug capital tax, consisting of paid-in share capital plus disclosed and hidden reserves after deductible participations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only capital effectively allocated to the Swiss permanent establishment is reportable; intra-group financing routed through Zug without substance is recharacterized as hidden equity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend distribution declaration and Swiss withholding tax remittance summary for Verrechnungssteuer purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the gross dividend, recipient jurisdiction, and date of payment; the 35% withholding tax must be remitted to the ESTV within 30 days of maturity and treaty relief is applied through refund or prior clearance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is sanctioned by reminder fees of CHF 100 to CHF 300 per reminder, statutory default interest accruing on unpaid assessments, and ex officio assessment where the return is not delivered; procedural non-submission can attract fines up to CHF 10,000 and deliberate concealment triggers tax evasion or fraud proceedings with restitution, penalty up to 100% of the evaded tax, and imprisonment for aggravated fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) withheld at source on gross dividend distributions from the AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial shareholders invoke the applicable double tax agreement by filing a refund application with the ESTV, generally within three years after the calendar year of distribution, submitting the home-state tax residence certificate, the AG dividend certificate, and a participation certificate; a prior ESTV clearance ruling may allow the AG to pay dividends at the reduced treaty rate where the ownership threshold, typically 10%, and the minimum holding period are established.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No Swiss withholding tax is levied on arm's-length royalties or ordinary intra-group loan interest; a 35% statutory WHT applies to interest on debentures, bond-type collective financing, and substitute instruments. Under modern Swiss DTAs, royalties and contractually genuine interest are generally taxable only in the residence state with 0% source WHT, subject to beneficial ownership and economic substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law establishes no codified documentation threshold; in practice the Zug administration expects contemporaneous OECD Local File documentation for controlled cross-border transactions exceeding CHF 1,000,000 per counterparty per fiscal year and Master File documentation for multinational groups above CHF 50 million consolidated turnover; absence of documentation shifts the burden of proof and increases penalty exposure on transfer pricing adjustments.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no dedicated Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the UAE regime, but the OECD substance-over-form doctrine, BEPS Action 6 principal-purpose test, Swiss anti-avoidance case law, and Verrechnungssteuer substance requirements apply. The AG manufacturing custom mechanical keyboard caps must maintain genuine premises and qualified employees in Zug, hold board decisions locally, control procurement, logistics, and IP functions in Switzerland, and document the functions, assets, and risks supporting its arm's-length manufacturing margin.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Tax Fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully submitting incomplete records, suppressing Shopify and Stripe payment revenues, overstating goods bought, fabricating invoices, or concealing foreign bank accounts linked to keycap sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the evaded federal and Zug cantonal tax, default interest, and an administrative fine of up to 100% of the evaded tax; criminal tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and additional court fines under federal and cantonal tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns, instruct the concealment, or knowingly benefit from evasion are prosecuted as individual offenders and can face detention pending trial, travel restrictions, civil restitution orders, and forced personal assets seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Granting shareholders or affiliated persons non-arm's-length advantages such as excessive management fees, unbalanced royalty payments, interest-free upstream loans, or private use of company assets deducted as business expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the expense, upward profit adjustment, recharacterization as a distribution triggering 35% Swiss withholding tax, plus interest and penalties on the deemed dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who authorized the unauthorized advantage are jointly and severally liable for the un-withheld WHT and for restitution to the company in insolvency under Swiss withholding tax and company law; discharge is not accepted in tax fraud investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Documenting artificial markups for keycap manufacturing, failing to prepare a comparability analysis, omitting local and master files for cross-border resin purchases and international sales, or using circular payments with tax-haven distributors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length result, secondary adjustments recharacterizing the excess as a constructive distribution with 35% WHT, reassessment interest, and fines for failure to keep proper business records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve misleading transfer pricing policies can be sued by the company for damages, held liable for the extra tax assessed and penalties where they acted against published OECD guidance, and personally fined when they sign false declarations to the Zug authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Shopping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG as a mailbox entity with no payroll, no physical production or inventory in Zug, board meetings held abroad, and profit shifting to secure Zug tax benefits, the federal participation exemption, or DTA withholding tax reductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of profits to the jurisdiction of effective management, denial of DTA benefits under the principal-purpose test, revocation of the participation exemption, withholding tax on deemed distributions, and reassessment for open limitation periods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Founders and directors remain civilly liable for unpaid tax and are exposed to criminal prosecution for tax omission; international cooperation and search warrants may lift Swiss banking secrecy and trigger travel restrictions pending the criminal tax case.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large unexplained cash payments for wholesale keyboard cap batches, issuing false invoices to shell resellers, keeping parallel cash books, or structuring Shopify and Stripe settlements through private accounts to conceal revenue from Swiss tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Confiscation of proceeds, disqualification from commercial filings, fines under the Swiss Criminal Code, and aggravated money-laundering charges where the director knew the funds derived from tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are prosecuted as natural persons, risk imprisonment, and face asset freezes and travel bans until the penalty and confiscation order is secured; the corporate veil is ineffective in laundering investigations.
